workshop_summary: Workshop output (summary): baseline QPS = 35 req/s (steady-state), median tokens/request = 120, baseline tokens/sec = ~4200. Peak burst observed in traces: short bursts up to 110 req/s for 30-90s (avg tokens/request during bursts = 95) => peak tokens/sec ~10450. Latency targets: p95 <= 120ms for single-turn chat (<=512 tokens), p99 <= 300ms for interactive flows; for long-generation jobs (>=1024 tokens) target p95 <= 800ms. Recommended dedicated pool: 4 x H100-equivalent GPUs for steady-state with autoscale + 2x burst nodes (same instance type) to cover peak headroom. If customer prefers A10-series cost profile, estimate 8 x A10s reserved with similar peak cushion. Throughput guarantees: propose committed throughput slab of 6k tokens/sec sustained with 2x burst headroom to 12k tokens/sec. KV/prefix cache sizing: allocate ~120GB shared cache to keep 95% of active sessions warm. Notes: batching window should be tuned to 8-12ms to balance latency/cost.
sla_and_negotiation_notes: Customer insists on explicit p95 latency SLO in contract for chat flows; wants financial credits for outages > 99.9% uptime.
Procurement requested a teardown of SLA credit calculation and a security appendix for KMS key custody (must support customer-managed keys).

We proposed service tiers: Standard (best-effort, lower price), Enterprise Dedicated (SLA-backed latency & throughput guarantees) — customer leaning to Enterprise Dedicated with 12-month reserved commit.
technical_requirements_summary: Model preferences: preference for 13B-70B open models; willing to use quantized variants for cost reductions but needs regen-quality validation.
Routing/fallback: require deterministic fallback to quantized variant in a different AZ when capacity constrained; customer wants explicit failover tests in contract.
Monitoring: token-level billing + per-route latency traces required for internal chargeback.
Retention/residency: logs stored EU/US by dataset; some datasets must remain in us-east-1 only.
